```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)

# Set to TRUE only when you want to (re)write the PDFs in ../figures/pdfs/
save_pdfs <- FALSE

# Figure filenames start with the Rmd's name, e.g. alpha-glucosidase-2026-08-17_Alina-boxplot-1
fig_prefix <- sub("\\.Rmd$", "", knitr::current_input())

# PDF device that writes straight into ../figures/pdfs/ (gitignored), same filename as the PNG
pdf_to_folder <- function(file, width, height, ...) {
  grDevices::pdf(file.path("../figures/pdfs", basename(file)),
                 width = width, height = height, ...)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  fig.path = paste0("../figures/knitted_mds/", fig_prefix, "-"),
  dev     = if (save_pdfs) c("png", "pdf_to_folder") else "png",
  fig.ext = if (save_pdfs) c("png", "pdf")           else "png"
)
```

```{r libraries, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(knitr)

# Folder holding the plate-reader export (edit if it lives elsewhere)
data_dir    <- "../data"
results_dir <- "../results"
```

# Overview

Sigma-Aldrich alpha-Glucosidase Activity Assay Kit (MAK123), read on the
Multiskan SkyHigh at 405 nm, kinetic reads every 6 s for 20 min at 25.5 °C.

**Storage test (24 h).** Susceptible SLCMAD *Culex pipiens* larvae, 2 single
larvae per method, stored for about 24 hours before the assay in one of
three media, either at room temperature or frozen at -80 °C:

- **80% EtOH**
- **Tris**
- **PBS**
- **Live**: not stored

Two wells are marked "\* Samples could have been switched" on the plate map:
E1 (Tris, frozen) and G1 (PBS, frozen). They are kept as labelled; see the
notes.

**Activity.** From the kit:

$$\text{Activity (U/L)} = \frac{A405_{final} - A405_{initial}}{A405_{calibrator} - A405_{water}} \times 250$$

- *initial* = first kinetic read (t = 0); *final* = last read (t = 20 min)
- calibrator and water = their own reads at 20 min
- If A405_final > 1.0, the kit says to dilute with water and repeat. Set
  `dilution` in the plate map for any re-run well and the result is
  multiplied back up.

One unit hydrolyzes 1.0 µmole substrate per minute at pH 7.0.

# Plate map

From Alina's plate map.

```{r plate-map}
infile    <- file.path(data_dir, "Kinetic Abs @ 405 2026-07-10 09-15-51.xlsx")
run_label <- "2026-07-10"

water_well <- "A1"   # H2O control
cal_well   <- "A2"   # calibrator

medium_order <- c("80% EtOH", "Tris", "PBS", "Live")
temp_order   <- c("Room temp", "Frozen -80 °C")

plate_map <- data.frame(
  well   = c("B1","B2", "C1","C2", "D1","D2", "E1","E2", "F1","F2", "G1","G2", "H1","H2"),
  medium = c(rep("80% EtOH", 4), rep("Tris", 4), rep("PBS", 4), rep("Live", 2)),
  temp   = c(rep(rep(temp_order, each = 2), 3), NA, NA),
  maybe_switched = FALSE,
  dilution = 1
)
plate_map$maybe_switched[plate_map$well %in% c("E1", "G1")] <- TRUE
plate_map$group <- ifelse(is.na(plate_map$temp), "Live",
                          paste(plate_map$medium, plate_map$temp, sep = ", "))
```

# Colors

All larvae are SLCMAD, so every point uses the SLCMAD color from the Lsph
probit figures: open circles for room temperature, filled for frozen,
diamond for live.

```{r colors}
slcmad_col <- "#005A9C"
colony_colors <- c(Yellow   = "#B8860B",   # mustard gold (was #E6AB02)
                   SLCMAD   = "#005A9C",   # deeper blue  (was #0072B2)
                   Green    = "#007A55",   # deeper green (was #009E73)
                   Orange   = "#D04A00",   # burnt orange (was #E66100)
                   White    = "#5E3C99",   # deeper purple (was #7B5EA7)
                   "Wild R" = "grey20")
```

# Data

The "Raw data 405 nm" sheet has one row per well per read (well, wavelength,
absorbance, time in seconds). The header row is found by name, because the
number of blank rows above it differs between exports.

```{r read-data}
raw <- suppressWarnings(
  read_excel(infile, sheet = "Raw data 405 nm", col_names = FALSE,
             col_types = c("text", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric")))
names(raw)[1:4] <- c("well", "wavelength", "abs", "time_s")
header_row <- which(raw$well == "Well")[1]
raw <- as.data.frame(raw[(header_row + 1):nrow(raw), ])
raw <- raw[!is.na(raw$well) & !is.na(raw$abs), ]
raw$well <- gsub(" ", "", raw$well)            # "A 1" -> "A1"
raw <- raw[order(raw$well, raw$time_s), ]

table(raw$well)                                # reads per well (expect 201)
```

# Activity

```{r activity}
first_abs <- tapply(raw$abs, raw$well, function(x) x[1])
last_abs  <- tapply(raw$abs, raw$well, function(x) x[length(x)])

water_20 <- last_abs[[water_well]]
cal_20   <- last_abs[[cal_well]]
denom    <- cal_20 - water_20
cat(sprintf("Calibrator (%s) at 20 min = %.4f\nWater (%s) at 20 min = %.4f\n",
            cal_well, cal_20, water_well, water_20))

agc <- plate_map
agc$A405_initial <- as.numeric(first_abs[agc$well])
agc$A405_final   <- as.numeric(last_abs[agc$well])
agc$activity_U_L <- (agc$A405_final - agc$A405_initial) / denom * 250 * agc$dilution
agc$over_1       <- agc$A405_final > 1.0

group_order <- c(as.vector(t(outer(medium_order[1:3], temp_order, paste, sep = ", "))), "Live")
agc$group   <- factor(agc$group, levels = group_order)

if (any(agc$over_1))
  warning("A405_final > 1.0 in wells: ", paste(agc$well[agc$over_1], collapse = ", "),
          " -- kit says dilute and repeat.")

write.csv(agc, file.path(results_dir, paste0("agc_activity_", run_label, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)
kable(agc, digits = 3)
```

## Summary by storage method

```{r summary}
agc_summary <- data.frame(
  group    = group_order,
  n        = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$group, length)),
  mean_U_L = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$group, mean)),
  min_U_L  = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$group, min)),
  max_U_L  = as.numeric(tapply(agc$activity_U_L, agc$group, max))
)
agc_summary$pct_of_live <- 100 * agc_summary$mean_U_L /
                           agc_summary$mean_U_L[agc_summary$group == "Live"]

write.csv(agc_summary, file.path(results_dir, paste0("agc_summary_", run_label, ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)
kable(agc_summary, digits = 1)
```

## Comparison with live (Dunnett)

As in Alina's analysis: one-way ANOVA, then Dunnett's test comparing each
storage method with live. Needs the `multcomp` package. With only 2 larvae
per group, these tests have very little power; treat them as descriptive.

```{r dunnett}
agc$group_vs_live <- relevel(agc$group, ref = "Live")
anova_model <- aov(activity_U_L ~ group_vs_live, data = agc)
summary(anova_model)

if (requireNamespace("multcomp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dunnett <- multcomp::glht(anova_model,
                            linfct = multcomp::mcp(group_vs_live = "Dunnett"))
  summary(dunnett)
} else {
  message("multcomp not installed; install.packages('multcomp') for Dunnett's test.")
}
```

# Plot

With 2 larvae per group, each larva is shown with a bar at the group mean
instead of a box. Room temperature (open) and frozen (filled) sit side by
side for each medium; the dashed line is the live mean. \* marks the two
wells that may have been switched.

```{r dotplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
x_medium <- setNames(seq_along(medium_order), medium_order)
offset   <- c("Room temp" = -0.18, "Frozen -80 °C" = 0.18)
agc$x <- x_medium[agc$medium] + ifelse(is.na(agc$temp), 0, offset[agc$temp])
agc$x[is.na(agc$x)] <- x_medium[["Live"]]

means <- aggregate(cbind(activity_U_L, x) ~ group, data = agc, FUN = mean)
live_mean <- means$activity_U_L[means$group == "Live"]

par(mar = c(4.5, 4.8, 3, 1))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0.5, length(medium_order) + 0.5),
     ylim = c(0, max(agc$activity_U_L) * 1.15),
     xaxt = "n", las = 1, xlab = "Storage medium (about 24 h)",
     ylab = expression(alpha*"-glucosidase activity (U/L)"),
     main = expression(alpha*"-glucosidase activity by storage method (07/10/2026)"))
axis(1, at = x_medium, labels = medium_order)
abline(h = live_mean, lty = 2, col = "grey50")
segments(means$x - 0.12, means$activity_U_L, means$x + 0.12, means$activity_U_L,
         col = slcmad_col, lwd = 2)
pch <- ifelse(agc$medium == "Live", 18, ifelse(agc$temp == "Room temp", 1, 16))
points(agc$x, agc$activity_U_L, pch = pch, cex = 1.4, col = slcmad_col, lwd = 1.5)
text(agc$x[agc$maybe_switched], agc$activity_U_L[agc$maybe_switched],
     "*", pos = 4, cex = 1.3)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, pch = c(1, 16, 18), col = slcmad_col,
       legend = c("Room temp", "Frozen -80 °C", "Live (dashed line = mean)"))
mtext("SLCMAD single larvae, n = 2 per group", side = 3, line = 0.2,
      cex = 0.8, col = "grey40")
```

# QC: kinetic curves

Each well's A405 over the 20 min. The formula uses only the first and last
reads, so a well whose signal jumps around can shift its activity value.
Water and calibrator are dashed grey.

```{r kinetics, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
medium_lty <- setNames(1:4, medium_order)
par(mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
plot(NA, xlim = range(raw$time_s) / 60, ylim = range(raw$abs), las = 1,
     xlab = "Time (min)", ylab = "A405", main = "Kinetic reads, 07/10/2026")
for (w in unique(raw$well)) {
  d <- raw[raw$well == w, ]
  i <- match(w, agc$well)
  if (is.na(i)) {
    lines(d$time_s / 60, d$abs, col = "grey60", lty = 2)
  } else {
    lines(d$time_s / 60, d$abs, col = slcmad_col,
          lty = medium_lty[[agc$medium[i]]],
          lwd = if (identical(agc$temp[i], "Frozen -80 °C")) 2 else 1)
  }
}
legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
       legend = c(medium_order, "thick = frozen", "water / calibrator"),
       col = c(rep(slcmad_col, 5), "grey60"), lty = c(1:4, 1, 2),
       lwd = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1))
```

```{r notes-values, include=FALSE}
m <- setNames(round(agc_summary$mean_U_L), agc_summary$group)
p <- setNames(round(agc_summary$pct_of_live), agc_summary$group)
```

# Notes

*Summary for Alina and the lab, written 10/22/2026.*

- **Results (2 larvae each, about 24 h storage).** Live averaged
  `r m[["Live"]]` U/L. Frozen PBS read highest (`r m[["PBS, Frozen -80 °C"]]`
  U/L, `r p[["PBS, Frozen -80 °C"]]`% of live); frozen 80% EtOH and room-temp
  PBS were somewhat below live (`r p[["80% EtOH, Frozen -80 °C"]]`% and
  `r p[["PBS, Room temp"]]`%); Tris at either temperature and room-temp EtOH
  were lowest. With n = 2, none of this is conclusive.
- **Frozen PBS above live.** One possible explanation is that freezing and
  thawing breaks up tissue and releases more enzyme into the homogenate.
  That's a guess; it would need more larvae to test.
- **E1 and G1 ("could have been switched").** As labelled, both frozen-PBS
  larvae read high (`r round(agc$activity_U_L[agc$well == "G1"])` and
  `r round(agc$activity_U_L[agc$well == "G2"])` U/L) and both frozen-Tris
  larvae read low (`r round(agc$activity_U_L[agc$well == "E1"])` and
  `r round(agc$activity_U_L[agc$well == "E2"])` U/L). Swapping E1 and G1 would
  give each group one high and one low value, so the data fit the labels as
  recorded better than the swap.
- **Compared with 07/31.** After about a week, 100% EtOH at -80 °C kept only
  about a tenth of live activity and PBS at room temp about a third, while
  glycerol/PBS kept all of it. Here, after 24 h, the losses were smaller, and
  the EtOH was 80%, not 100%. Storage time and EtOH strength both seem to
  matter; glycerol/PBS (tested on 07/31) is the method with the best support
  so far.
